The paper discusses the difference in radar cross section (σ) definitions between microwave and optical frequencies.
At microwave frequencies, σ is based on a lossless isotropic sphere.
At optical frequencies, σ is based on a lossless diffuse flat plate.
An isotropic sphere scatters radiation uniformly in all directions (4π sr).
The scattered intensity from an isotropic sphere is J_s = P / 4π.
For a diffuse flat plate, the scattered intensity is J_s = P / π.
The factor difference between the two definitions is four.
The microwave radar cross section formula is σ_i = 4π (J / H).
The optical radar cross section formula is σ_d = π (J / H).
The factor-of-four difference affects the interpretation of radar cross section values.
The flat plate is assumed to be perpendicular to the transmitter beam.
The far field relationship is assumed for both standards.
The paper emphasizes the importance of using the correct standard for accurate radar cross section interpretation.
The common form of the laser radar range equation is derived in the paper.
The reference for the microwave radar definition is L. N. Ridenour, Radar System Engineering (1947), p. 21.
